title: The append path, its authorisation and its 404 semantics are a target choice, and the case scope check becomes a cross-service call
source: Legacy RWB-E1-066 section 12 Published interface (P1) and section 5 X4; API Specification v4 path /cases/{caseId}/interactions (x-module P3) and schemas Interaction, InteractionRequest and InteractionPage; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json entries interaction, processed_event, outbox_event and idempotency_key; _work/msr/wp/B-P1-02.md story line RWB-P1-E1066-APP; Template and Rules v1 R3, R7.3 and R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria AC7; 12.1; 12.2; 13
description: The legacy writer was an in-process Java interface, InteractionLedgerWriter.append(), called inside the caller's transaction (legacy section 12). It had no path, no status code of its own beyond the ones the P3 handler produced, no Idempotency-Key header, and no client-side scope check: the scope was a local read of recovery_case in the same database. The Work Package turns the writer into a REST operation of rwb-source-data and gives the story an AC7 whose case lookup now crosses to rwb-case, but no source states the path of the operation, the error status of a repeated key with a different body, or how a 404 from rwb-case is told apart from a case outside the caller's scope. The API specification keeps the append under x-module P3 at /cases/{caseId}/interactions, which contradicts the ruling that the ledger and its writer are P1's.
evidence: Legacy section 12 Published interface (P1) with the Java records and the Propagation.MANDATORY note; legacy section 5 X4 with 404 and MSG-P4-003; API Specification v4 /cases/{caseId}/interactions with x-module P3; ownership.json interaction owner P1 with its ruling; Architecture v5 slide 15 IN line for rwb-source-data, which names no interactions path
proposed: Fix the append as POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/interactions on the P1 service base, with Idempotency-Key required, 404 with MSG-P4-003 for both a case rwb-case does not know and a case outside the caller's scope, and 422 on a repeated key with a different body. The case check is one hop to GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} with a 2 s budget, and the read that answers 201 is GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/interactions/{entryId} on the same base. Revisit only if the next API Specification moves the append to P1 explicitly.

title: The interaction ledger is P1's by ruling while the API specification keeps the ledger path under x-module P3, and no P1 resource path is given
source: API Specification v4 path /cases/{caseId}/interactions, GET and POST, x-module P3, and the Interaction, InteractionRequest and InteractionPage schemas; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json entries interaction and efs_ledger_outcome with the P1 ruling; Legacy RWB-E1-066 section 12 Endpoint used (P3, API-P3-015) and Published interface (P1); Architecture v5 slides 29 and 41; _work/msr/wp/B-P1-02.md story line RWB-P1-E1066-CON
section: 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 and AC5; 10 Authority; 12.1; 12.2; 12.8; 19 Out of scope
description: Two sources disagree on who owns the ledger path. The API Specification v4 declares GET and POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions with x-module P3 and describes them as the case interaction ledger; the R-PREC default ruling and DP-18 give the interaction ledger to rwb-source-data, and the Ownership Map records interaction and efs_ledger_outcome as P1's with a ruling that the case timeline stays with P3 and that consumers read the ledger through P1's contract. The legacy story compounds this: its writer is a published P1 interface while the endpoint it documents is P3's POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions. No source gives the path of a P1 ledger resource, and the Work Package asks the contract story to record the split and the read contract.
evidence: API Specification v4 /cases/{caseId}/interactions, GET and POST, x-module P3; ownership.json interaction owner P1 with the ruling that the ledger and the intake rule stay with rwb-source-data while the timeline and the interaction API stay with rwb-case; legacy section 12 Endpoint used (P3, API-P3-015) beside Published interface (P1); Architecture v5 slide 41 P1 row
proposed: The contract fixes P1 as the owner of POST /interactions, GET /interactions and GET /interactions/{entryId} on /api/recovery/source-data/v1, and names the P3 GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions as a consumer that reads the ledger through the P1 read interface of RWB-P1-E1068-APP, never as a second ledger. A P3 timeline that needs a ledger row calls the P1 contract, and no P3 table holds a ledger entry.

title: No source gives the deployment values, the alert thresholds, the probe timings or the incident route of the ledger writer
source: Legacy RWB-E1-066 sections 12 and 13; Architecture v5 slide 11 (2 s REST budget) and DP-09 (retry topics); _work/msr/wp/B-P1-02.md story line RWB-P1-E1066-OPS; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s16 and R9; the Error and Message Standard as cited by RWB-P2-E2034-OPS
section: 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria AC4 and AC5; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages; 19 Out of scope
description: The legacy story has no deployment section: the ledger table, the writer and the incident hook were part of one monolith release, and its only operational statement is the incident code LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED. The Work Package asks for six deployment criteria with a chart, a migration step, a flag, five series and three alerts, but no values file, replica count, resource size, probe timing, alert threshold, window, alert text or routing rule for the ledger writer exists in the source set, and the Error and Message Standard names no message for the trigger alert.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-066 sections 12 and 13 name the incident code LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED and the flag rwb.dataengine.ledger-writer only; Architecture v5 slide 11 gives the 2 s REST budget and DP-09 the retry topics, and neither gives a threshold, a window, a probe timing or a route; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s16 requires an NFR level and R9 the placeholder
proposed: Fix the artefact names and the rule that every value is an environment value, keep MSG-P1-022 for the append failure alert and the incident code LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED for the incident alert, and carry the thresholds, the windows, the probe timings and the routes as environment values, with the trigger alert text as the placeholder until the Error and Message Standard names it.
